text: Fixed interpolation, spline and Haar controls Small fixed examples separate nodes, representation and rounding; C2 continuity and shape preservation; and boundary extension and shifts. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-approximation-controls-2026-11-25 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Runge interpolation: nodes, representation and rounding Interpolate the Runge and absolute-value functions on fixed equispaced and Lobatto-like nodes, and compare with Clenshaw evaluation. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless interval [-1,1], degrees 8, 16 and 32, and 2048 fixed midpoints. Actual binary64 nodes, data and weights define the discrete problem. Editorial clarification A sampled maximum error is not a proof of a continuous uniform norm. Closed weights and discrete orthogonality on rounded nodes are not treated as exact. No arbitrary-degree or all-point stability guarantee is made. Adopted numerical method Implement the second barycentric formula and a full-coefficient Clenshaw recurrence. Natural and clamped splines versus PCHIP Compare C2 continuity and shape preservation on three fixed data sets: a monotone plateau, a cubic and a straight line. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use actual binary64 knots and values. Natural conditions set both endpoint second derivatives to zero; clamped conditions prescribe the first derivatives from the input. Editorial clarification PCHIP is generally C1, not necessarily C2. Best approximation, extrapolation and noise smoothing are outside scope. A SciPy comparison does not substitute for reading the original papers. Adopted numerical method Solve a cubic B-spline collocation system and evaluate it with de Boor recursion. A separate path implements PCHIP harmonic slopes, endpoint limiting and Hermite evaluation. No de Boor original full-text claim. SciPy is a secondary numerical companion; the rational second-derivative system is the independent reference. Haar multiresolution: boundaries, shifts and thresholds Apply three-level Haar analysis to short signals of lengths 17 and 32, separating one-sample shifts from odd-length boundary handling. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries At each odd-length level append the first sample for periodic extension or the last for symmetric extension, then crop during synthesis. Apply threshold 0.2 only to detail coefficients. Editorial clarification Limited to Haar, without longer filters or image compression. General symmetric extension is not assumed orthonormal. Shift invariance is not required; shift-dependent differences are retained. Sample indices are not physical spatial coordinates. This is a finite-signal map with declared boundary handling. Adopted numerical method Implement pair-sum and pair-difference filters, downsampling and inverse pyramids.
